We break up the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }\frac{2x}{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{2x}{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{2x}{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x
$$

First, we calculate the antiderivative using a substitution. Let  $u={x}^{2}$,  then $\text{d}u=2x\text{d}x.$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{{e}^{u}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\int {e}^{-u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-{e}^{-u}+C \\  & =-{e}^{-{x}^{2}}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We now evaluate the first of the improper integrals, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{2x}{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{0}\frac{2x}{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{(-{e}^{-{x}^{2}})|}_{a}^{0} \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }(-{e}^{0}-(-{e}^{-{a}^{2}})) \\  & =-1+0 \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the integrand is an **odd** function. This means that we can immediately deduce that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{2x}{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x=1.
$$

Therefore, since both improper integrals exist, we conclude that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }\frac{2x}{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{2x}{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{2x}{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-1+1 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
